Apple is less than two weeks away from unveiling a brand-new smart display, according to a new report from Bloomberg. The report also fills in the design details of Apple's much-anticipated smart home hub.

Bloomberg reports that the home hub will feature a 6-inch square display. The overall design is reminiscent of the classic iMac G4, characterised by a hemispherical base supporting the screen with a metal arm.

According to Mark Gurman, the device is "about as thick as an iPhone," with quarter-inch black bezels similar to older iPads. The body features rounded corners, "with no sharp edges anywhere."

Here are some of the design details mentioned in the report:

  • The body comes in Apple's "standard gray aluminium finish," and features a "rubber base on the bottom for placing on a table."
  • There's a USB-C port for power, with no built-in battery, meaning it must remain plugged in at all times.
  • The bottom of the device is a "circular metal base with speaker holes that go around in rings."
  • The display is connected to the base via a "polished metal arm."
  • Users can tilt it forward or backward to adjust the angle.
  • There are no volume or power buttons on the device.
  • There's a FaceTime camera on the front, with no camera on the back.

Bloomberg also mentions another version of the home hub, "designed to be mounted on a wall." This version is also powered by USB-C and features a "thin square base beneath the display that houses speakers and microphones." According to the report, the base "sits flush against the wall, below the display."

You can read the full report on the Bloomberg website. What do you think of Apple's home hub product? Planning to pick one up (or even several)? Drop your thoughts in the comments.
